title: Manifest, version 0
description: How a managed repository describes itself. Written as TOML. Every key is listed here: an unknown key is an error, so a misspelt one fails instead of being ignored.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema the manifest follows. A reader that does not know the version must refuse the manifest.

components.description: The buildable parts of the repository, keyed by name. At least one.

gates.description: The commands that decide whether a change may proceed, keyed by name.

name.description: A lower-case slug. Names appear in commands, labels and paths.

command.description: A program and its arguments, as a list. Never a single string: a string needs a shell to split it, and then quoting decides what runs.

path.description: A path or glob relative to the repository root, with forward slashes. It may not be absolute and may not contain a `..` segment, so it means the same thing in every checkout and cannot reach outside the repository.

toolchain.description: How to enter the repository's pinned toolchain.

wrapper.description: Put in front of every command in this manifest.

inside_env.description: The name of an environment variable that is set when the caller is already inside the toolchain. When it is set, the wrapper is not applied.

component.description: One buildable part of the repository.

pack.description: The Athenaeum pack that holds this component's stack knowledge.

root.description: The directory its commands run in.

paths.description: Globs for the files that belong to it. A change is attributed to a component by these.

generated.description: Globs for files that are generated and must not be edited by hand.

lint.description: Its format and lint checks, each a command that changes nothing and fails on a finding.

gate.description: A command, run from the repository root, that decides whether a change may proceed.

when_paths.description: Globs. The gate applies only to a change that touches a matching file. Absent means it applies to every change.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the gate may run before it is stopped and counted as failed. Required, because a gate with no limit can hold a workload open for ever.

result.description: How the gate reports. `exit-code`, the default: zero is a pass. `json`: the command also writes a structured result that the caller reads.

docs.description: Where the repository keeps the documents a skill may need. A skill asks for a document by these names and never hard-codes a path.

stories.description: Files or directories holding user stories.

mapping.description: The document that maps stories to the code that implements them.

goals.description: Documents stating what the product is for and what it has ruled out.
